title: Representing a graph: adjacency matrix
summary: A V × V grid: a 1 in row u, column v means an edge between u and v.

checkpoints.text: 5 vertices, numbered 0 to 4, and a 5 × 5 grid of zeros: no edges yet.
Edge 0–1. The graph is undirected, so the edge is stored twice: row 0, column 1 and row 1, column 0. The graph view on the right is drawn from the grid.
All five edges are in. The grid is symmetric across its diagonal, which is how you can tell an undirected graph from a directed one.
To list the neighbours of vertex 3, the loop reads its whole row, one column at a time.
Neighbours of 3: 1 2 4. Checking one edge takes O(1), but listing neighbours always reads V cells, and the grid uses V² memory even when there are few edges.
